chunks: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Why do you see those whom God, Mighty and Majestic, has dispatched for wretchedness upon the people of misguidance from the armies of the Satans and their consorts to be more numerous than what you see of the Caliph of God whom He dispatched for justice and righteousness from among the Angels? It was said: O Abu Ja'far, how can anything be more numerous than the Angels? He said: As God, Mighty and Majestic, has willed.

The questioner said: O Abu Ja'far, if I were to narrate this hadith to some of the Shi'a, they would deny it. He said: How would they deny it? He said: They would say that the Angels are more numerous than the Satans. He said: You are right. Understand from me what I am saying: there is not a single day or night except that all the Jinn and Satans visit the imams of misguidance, and an equal number of Angels visits the Imam of Guidance — until when the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) comes, Angels descend during it to the Master of the Command in a number that God, Mighty and Majestic, has created — or said: destined — from among the Satans as their equal number.

Then they visit the master of misguidance and bring him fabrications and lies, until perhaps he wakes up in the morning saying: I saw such-and-such. But if one were to ask the Master of the Command about that, he would say: You saw a Satan who informed you of such-and-such, until he would interpret it for him and make known to him the misguidance upon which he stands.

And by God, whoever believes in the Night of Power knows that it belongs to us exclusively, by virtue of the saying of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) to Ali (peace be upon him) when death drew near him: This is your guardian after me — if you obey him you will be rightly guided. But whoever does not believe in what is in the Night of Power is a denier, and whoever believes in the Night of Power while holding a view other than ours — it is not permissible for him in truth except to say that it belongs to us; and whoever does not say so is a liar.

Surely God, Mighty and Majestic, is too exalted to send down the Command with the Spirit and the Angels to a disbeliever, a transgressor. If they say that it descends to the Caliph who claims that authority, then their saying is worthless; and if they say that it does not descend to anyone, it cannot be that something descends upon nothing; and if they say — and they will say — that this is nothing, then they have gone astray with a far-reaching straying.

key_terms.أَئِمَّةُ الضَّلَالَةِ: Imams of misguidance — false leaders who usurped authority
key_terms.أَجْنَادُ الشَّيَاطِينِ: Armies of the Satans — spiritual forces of evil that support false leaders
key_terms.خَلِيفَةُ اللَّهِ: Caliph/Vicegerent of God — the true Imam appointed by God
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Power/Predetermination (Laylat al-Qadr) — the blessed night in Ramadan described in Surah 97, when divine decrees are determined
key_terms.وَلِيُّ الْأَمْرِ: Master/Guardian of the Command — the legitimate Imam of the Ahlulbayt

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about Laylat al-Qadr and the Imamate?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) explains in a detailed discourse that Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Power from Surah 97) belongs exclusively to the Imams of the Ahlulbayt. He clarifies an apparent paradox: while Angels are greater in number than Satans overall, on every day and night the Satans visit the imams of misguidance while an equal number of Angels visits the Imam of Guidance. On Laylat al-Qadr specifically, the Angels descend to the Master of the Command (the Imam), while an equal number of Satans visit the false claimants, bringing them fabrications. This teaching was addressed to a questioner in the early Abbasid period when the question of legitimate religious and political authority was acutely contested.

en.sarwar: 8. The narrator has said that a man said to abu Ja‘far (a.s.), “O child of the Messenger of Allah, “Please do not be angry with m.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Why should I be angry?” The man said, “It is because of the question that like to ask you.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Ask your question.” He said, “Please do not be angry.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “I will not be angry.”

The man said, “Consider your words about the ‘Night of Determination’ in which the Spirit and the angels descent to the executors of the will (of Prophet). Do they bring them the command of which the Messenger of Allah had no knowledge or bring them the commands that the Messenger of Allah knew? As you know that the Messenger of Allah died and there was nothing of his knowledge that Ali (a.s.) had not heard it (and preserved).” Abu Ja‘far (a.s.) said, “Why should I bother with you and why someone let you come in?” He said, “Fate has let me come in, seeking religion.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Try to understand what I will say.” “When the Messenger of Allah was taken for a trip (by the angels) he did not come back before Allah, Majestic is Whose mention, taught him the knowledge of the things of the past and the things in future. A great deal of such knowledge was in a whole form the interpretation of which would have to come in the ‘Night of Determination’. In the same Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) had learned the knowledge in a whole form, the interpretation of which would have had to come in the ‘Night of Determination’ as was the case with the Messenger of Allah.” The man said, “Was there no interpretation of the whole available?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “It was available but it comes through the commands of Allah in the ‘Night of Determination’ to the Prophet the executor of his will telling them to do so and so. It is for the matters of which they already had knowledge, but they receive the command as how to act in it.” The man said, “Explain it to me.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “The Messenger of Allah, before his death had a whole of knowledge with its interpretation.” You said, “What was that which that would come to him in the ‘Night of Determination’?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “It was the command and ease in what he already knew.” The man questioning said, “What then happens to them in the ‘Night of Determination’ is a knowledge other than what they knew before.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “This is what they are commanded not to tell to anyone. No one knows the interpretation of what you just asked except Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High. The man questioning asked, “Do the executors of the know what the prophets know?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “No, because how would the executor of the will would know what is other than what is willed for.” The man asked, “Can we say that what one executor of the will may know may not be known another executor of the will?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “No, because no prophet dies before his knowledge is transferred into the executor of his will. The angels and the Spirit descend in the ‘Night of Determination’ with the judgment with which to judge among the people.” The man asked, “Is it that they did not know that judgment?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Yes, they knew it but they could not approve anything of it until they were commanded in the ‘Night of Determination’ how to accomplish them until the next year.” The man said, “O abu Ja‘far (a.s.) I can not deny this.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Those who deny it is not from us.”

The man asked, “O abu Ja‘far (a.s.), do you think in the ‘Night of Determination’ there would come things to the Holy Prophet (s.a.) that he did not know?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “It is not lawful for you to ask this. However, the knowledge of things in past and the knowledge of the things in future is as such that no prophet or the executor of the dies before the executor of will after him would know it. However, this know about which you ask is as such that Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, withholds and does not allow the executors of the will to know it by themselves.”
The man asked, “O child of the Messenger of Allah, how would I know that the ‘Night of Determination’ take place every year?”
The Imam (a.s.) said, “When the month of Ramadan comes read chapter 44 of the Holy Quran once every night. In the twenty third night you will see the confirmation of what you have asked for.”
